Though the floods eventually receded, the riverbeds remained, causing constant hardship for travelers and carriages during prolonged rains. Over a century, the mountain's Commoners and Mohist Disciples worked tirelessly, constructing several water-diversion mechanisms at the cost of hundreds of lives. I, merely following their lead, offer this humble record—carved in stone and cast in bronze—to honor those who sacrificed for the public good. May those who gave their lives for the people rest in peace.
